newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey expects $10 bln non-tax revenue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkey expects $10 bln non-tax revenue in 1997.

text.p: Turkish deputy PM Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday Turkey was expecting a $10 billon income from non-tax revenues and sell-offs in the envisaged zero-deficit 1997 budget, after $2 billion this year.

"A $2 billion income was raised from privatisations and non-tax revenues this year. We see this figure rising to $10 billion in 1997," Ciller told her conservative DYP deputies ahead of a censure motion to be debated in parliament later in the day.
She reiterated that the Islamist-led coalition had prepared a balanced budget draft for 1997, the first in Turkey since 1972.

"Taxes have risen by 120 percent (in 1996). This rapid rise continues in real terms without any changes in tax rates. Tax payers will increase to 20 million (in 1997)," Ciller said in response to criticisms that zero-deficit is unrealistic.

The draft budget, expected to be around 7,000 trillion lira after 3,511 trillion in 1996, must be presented to parliament's budgetary commission by Thursday at the latest for approval by parliament before the end of the year.
The 1996 deficit is expected to overshoot to 1,300 trillion lira from an original target of 861 trillion and compared to 317 trillion in 1995.
